rationale: Load-bearing tap injection points and companion files that anchor the pricing-availability passive observability system (docs/approved/pricing-availability-source-of-truth.md). Each entry is a 1-line TK injection in an upstream-shaped file that could be silently dropped by a future `git merge upstream/main`. Without these taps the model_availability table receives no data, availability status stays 'untested' forever, and the /pricing endpoint never decorates responses with real availability. This file is the single source of truth read by both scripts/preflight.sh and the upstream-merge-pr-shape workflow.

sentinels.rationale: gateway_handler.go has TK injection points across multiple flows: (1) failure taps at the Anthropic /v1/messages + Gemini /v1/messages error paths (TkRecordFailureFromErr), (2) the CatalogPolicy model-list projection on the whitelist path (tkFilterModelIDs), (3) the shape-preserving antigravity model filter (tkAntigravityDefaultModels), (4) the gemini /v1/models fallback re-point to the CatalogPolicy projection (tkGeminiDefaultModelsList) so the list converges with /pricing instead of returning the raw geminicli.DefaultModels (which still carried advertised_dead gemini-2.0-flash) — an upstream merge could silently revert this one-line branch back to the raw list and un-converge gemini /v1/models, (5) the pre-flight body-size guard on Messages + CountTokens entries (TkEvalBodyGuard) that fail-fast oversize requests before forward — see edge:us1 production data where opus-4-7 upstream rejects body >= ~940 KB with raw 403; and (6) the actionable-message enrichment for upstream 403 in handleFailoverExhausted + handleFailoverExhaustedSimple (TkEnrichForbiddenMessage). An upstream merge touching the forward-failed error handlers, the Models/AntigravityModels methods, or the entry hooks could silently drop any of these. If TkRecordFailureFromErr is lost, model_not_found failures from Anthropic and Gemini platforms stop being classified; if TkEvalBodyGuard is lost, claude-cli clients lose the pre-flight rejection and again hit upstream 403; if TkEnrichForbiddenMessage is lost, the 403 response collapses back to 'Upstream access forbidden, please contact administrator' without body-size hint.

The OpenAI chat completions forward-failure path (line ~247) records upstream 404/model_not_found errors. Without this tap, model_not_found failures from OpenAI-compat and newapi platform accounts are never classified, and those models stay 'untested' or 'stale' in the availability table instead of flipping to 'unreachable'. The test TestTkRecordFailureFromErr_ExtractsAndClassifies verifies the logic works but does NOT verify the tap call-site still exists in this handler. This PR also touches the OpenAI-compat sticky-session preparation hook in this upstream-shaped file; keeping this entry in the diff records that the availability tap was explicitly re-checked while routing code moved into the TK companion helper.

The Responses API forward-failure path records upstream errors for the /v1/responses endpoint. Without this tap, model failures on the Responses pathway are invisible to the availability system. Same regression risk as chat_completions: upstream could refactor the error path and silently drop the TK line. This entry also locks the TkEvalBodyGuard pre-flight hook so upstream churn on the /v1/responses entry cannot quietly remove body-size protection for OpenAI compat clients.

gemini_v1beta_handler.go has multiple TK injection points: (1) the failure tap on the /v1beta forward path that detects Google's 'Requested entity was not found' responses (TkRecordFailureFromErr), (2) the filtered Gemini fallback model list for the two static-fallback response paths (tkGeminiFallbackModelsList), (3) the pre-flight body-size guard before SelectAccount (TkEvalBodyGuard) — same data-driven motivation as anthropic opus-4-7 oversize rejection, and (4) the actionable-message enrichment for upstream 403 in mapGeminiUpstreamError's caller (TkEnrichForbiddenMessage). The Gemini handler is large and frequently touched by upstream; each TK injection is a 1-line addition easy to lose in merge conflict resolution.

gateway_service.go carries the success-path availability tap inside recordUsageCore (the 100%-hit path for all platform forwards) plus the TK 403 error-message enrichment in handleErrorResponse. Three sentinels: tkPricingAvailability (field declaration), RecordOutcome (success tap), and TkEnrichForbiddenMessage (403 client-message enrichment, replaces the default 'Upstream access forbidden, please contact administrator' with body-size hint). An upstream merge restructuring recordUsageCore or handleErrorResponse could silently remove any of these, collapsing the availability signal or regressing the 403 UX to the unhelpful default.
Success-path availability tap split from gateway_service.go into gateway_usage_billing.go.
403 client-message enrichment owner split from gateway_service.go.

This TK companion file is the single implementation of TkRecordFailureFromErr — the helper that extracts upstream HTTP status from UpstreamFailoverError and forwards it to the availability classifier. If this file is lost (e.g. an upstream merge that removes all untracked files), all 5 tap call sites compile against a missing function and the build fails. The file also contains the UpstreamFailoverError unwrap logic that makes model_not_found classification work correctly (R-004 fix from review-20260506).

The public /pricing endpoint prunes retired/unservable claude + gpt rows so customers only see models TokenKey can actually serve (empirical 2026-06-05 probe). The filter is PRESENTATION-ONLY — applied in GetPublicCatalog after BuildPublicCatalog, deliberately NOT in the shared parse (which also backs IsModelPriced billing/gateway filtering). An upstream merge that rewrites GetPublicCatalog could silently drop the call and restore the full unservable list (customers again pick claude-3-*/gpt-4o and hit 400/404). Pins the call site.

Single source for the empirically-servable native catalog sets, shared by the public /pricing presentation filter (FilterPublicCatalogToServable) and the Your-Menu unrestricted-account fallback (supportedCatalogModelIDsForPlatform). Losing the allowlist vars would silently widen both surfaces back to the full unservable set; losing the funcs breaks both call sites. The `servable-allowlist:begin/end` splice markers are load-bearing for ops/pricing/refresh-servable-allowlist.py (it rewrites the maps between them); an upstream merge that drops the markers would break the re-runnable refresh. The antigravity allowlist (supportedAntigravityCatalogModels: live Gemini set plus #1265 live Claude subset, with gpt-oss/dead/unpriced keys excluded from persisted account mappings) is hand-maintained from empirical probes; losing it silently reverts antigravity to passthrough or hides now-supported Claude IDs. The grok allowlist (supportedGrokCatalogModels: priced grok-imagine media + official-priced grok chat ids that returned 200 on the native grok edge probe) is likewise hand-maintained; losing it silently empties a grok group's 分组目录 again (2026-06-20 incident). Fifth-platform newapi long-tail display is delegated to tk_served_models_manifest_tk.go via isTkCuratedNewAPICatalogRowDisplayed; unknown vendors stay hidden until a universal mapping exists.

Runtime embed of tk_served_models.json — gates runtime newapi intent to manifest-listed models and public /pricing + Group Catalog display rows to manifest display=true only. Without it, priced overlay residue (deepseek-v3-2-251201), withdrawn SKUs (e.g. glm-4-7-251222 VolcEngine duplicate — GLM served via DashScope as glm-4.7), or entitlement-blocked GLM rows reappear on storefront/menu surfaces and mislead users into 400/429 requests while still looking priced.

R-003 single self-healing candidate source, shared by the admin model-whitelist selector (admin_service.GetGroupModelsListCandidates) and the per-user menu fallback (me_pricing). tkServableCandidateIDs draws anthropic/openai/gemini from the empirical allowlist and prunes structurally-gone models (model_not_found -> unreachable) via live model_availability (tkPruneStructurallyGoneIDs / tkAvailabilityStructurallyGone); antigravity/newapi keep canonical defaults. If an upstream merge or refactor drops this file, BOTH surfaces silently revert to the canonical defaults (claude.DefaultModels etc.) that still list retired / access-gated models like claude-fable-5 — exactly the hand-maintenance toil R-003 removed. Pins the function and its self-healing primitives.

GetGroupModelsListCandidates must call the self-healing tkServableCandidateIDs, NOT the canonical defaultModelsListCandidateIDs. The admin model-whitelist selector and GroupsView consume this endpoint; an upstream merge that reverts the call to the canonical defaults re-advertises retired / access-gated models (the R-003 regression) and renders the frontend self-heal inert. Pins the injection call site in the (upstream-shaped) admin service.

must_contain: withdrawn VolcEngine GLM SKU pruned from storefront
sentinels.rationale: Regression coverage for the public-catalog support filter: asserts retired/unservable claude+gpt rows are pruned, servable ones kept, curated newapi display=false rows are hidden, and unknown/unmapped vendors stay hidden until a universal mapping exists. TestSupportedCatalogModelIDsForPlatform (table-driven, covering anthropic/openai/antigravity/grok) and TestIsPublicCatalogModelSupported assert supportedCatalogModelIDsForPlatform / isPublicCatalogModelSupported against the live supported*CatalogModels maps by reference (any-key-from-map + explicit not-in-map probes) rather than duplicating each map's literal model list — so an SSOT allowlist refresh never requires a matching test edit, while an upstream merge that drops the filter functions or the test file itself still trips this sentinel. Pinned so an upstream merge that rewrites the catalog test file cannot silently drop the filter's regression guard. (This file also matches the *_tk_*.go hotspot via its _tk_test.go suffix, so the registry-update gate requires it to be tracked in a sentinel registry; pricing-availability is its correct domain.)

Interpreter for the data-owned official-list base-tax policy. Provider/vendor eligibility, multiplier, and bare-model fallback classification must all read the same immutable overlay snapshot; no provider/rate table may return to Go. Billing, public /pricing, and family fallback therefore change together on a validated runtime hot swap. Channel DB pricing remains outside this mechanism and is never re-taxed.

Executable SSOT for all currently taxed official-list providers. The embedded registry is the last-known-good fallback and a valid protected-main envelope replaces the whole snapshot atomically. Pinning every behavior-preserving provider row and the multiplier prevents an upstream merge from silently dropping one tax family while model prices continue to parse. New providers are added here, not in Go.

Pins the codex-auto-review SSOT regression at the runtime boundary. The behavior test injects deliberately wrong bundled prices and proves parsing still resolves the active registry owner, including base, priority, cache, and service-tier dimensions. Bundled/provider documents may drift as sensor evidence without becoming a second price owner or forcing a multi-file registry edit.

Pins provider billing, catalog presentation, and bare-model fallback behavior by deriving exhaustive providers and model matchers from the executable overlay policy. Tests retain only independent negative boundaries, so adding a provider or matcher changes the SSOT rather than requiring a second hand-maintained test list.

Provider model listing must read the immutable active registry in production. The mutable pricingData field remains only an upstream compatibility cache and direct-test fixture; reading it here lets a concurrent provider sync make the admin sync-models response stale after a successful hot reload.
Pins the regression proving constructor-created production services list models from the active registry rather than a stale provider compatibility cache after hot reload.

Catalog projection hook for the active complete registry. BuildPublicCatalog may still parse upstream metadata, but applyCatalogRegistrySnapshot must replace every external non-zero price and project intervals, tax, video, and DeepSeek policy from one immutable registry snapshot. Cache publication must also reject a response if that snapshot changed during construction. Channel pricing remains a higher explicit scope. Dropping either hook can make display and settlement disagree while both paths continue to compile.

BillingService pricing hooks: unknown zeroes fail closed, interval/thinking/media fields survive conversion, Imagen keeps flat billing, and compatibility aliases normalize. Production alias matching must resolve an active registry owner instead of using the legacy numeric Go fixture table. Not every registry row is a family alias; dropping the scoped hooks reintroduces price drift while broadening them changes fail-closed behavior for unrelated models.

Production alias owner: the mature legacy matcher may classify a requested model, but effective dimensions must be re-read from the active registry. The explicit fixture escape remains test-only, GPT-5.5 Pro resolves to the routed GPT-5.5 owner, and Kimi compatibility remains mapped without copying canonical price numbers here.

DeepSeek upstream peak-valley billing (Beijing 09:00-12:00 + 14:00-18:00, ×2). Overlay stores off-peak list prices; calculateTokenCost scales unit prices at BillingAt. Dropping this companion reverts to flat off-peak billing during upstream peak windows (≈50% under-charge vs DeepSeek direct API).

tkIsFlatPerImageModel is the imagen-scoped flat-billing predicate consumed by getDefaultImagePrice (billing_service.go, separately pinned): Imagen (Vertex) is priced by Google as a flat $/image per quality variant with NO 1K/2K/4K generation tier, so it must escape the 2K→×1.5 / 4K→×2 size-tier multiplier that is real only for genuine pixel-size models (Seedream). The `imagen-` prefix is the load-bearing scope — narrowing it (e.g. an upstream refactor that drops the predicate or changes the prefix) silently re-applies the ×1.5 markup to Imagen, the exact overcharge this exemption removed. Settlement AND the pre-flight HOLD both route through getDefaultImagePrice, so this one predicate keeps them consistent; the FE mirror is studioMediaPresentations.tk.ts flatPricePerImage (guarded by frontend-tk sentinels / studioMediaPresentations spec).

GPT-5.6 billing tier normalization is intentionally split from codex wire normalization (normalizeKnownOpenAICodexModel / normalizeCodexModel): upstream wire ids such as gpt-5.6-chat-latest must stay intact for OAuth transform while billing collapses chat-latest to the Sol tier key. Merging tier collapse back into normalizeKnownOpenAICodexModel silently breaks TestNormalizeCodexModel_Gpt53 and mis-bills chat-latest at the gpt-5.4 family floor. Pinning normalizeOpenAIBillingModel and the Sol collapse makes an upstream merge refactor fail CI instead of regressing wire vs billing separation.

The overlay gate validates media failure billing, critical price anchors, and executable base-tax policy. Tax config must have a bounded multiplier, unique normalized providers, and valid non-duplicated fallback matchers before either an embedded release or runtime sync can consume it.

Overwrite-protection gates for the media unpriced-reject guard: lock guard<->video-billing parity (billing semantics change must update the guard in the same change) and the empty-model fail-open premise (the OAuth default image model must stay priced in the shipped chain). Deleting these tests re-opens the silent-drift channels they close.

The served-models manifest drift guard asserts repository agreement for the thin intent layer: (A1) non-zero pricing, (A2) native allowlist or manifest-owned newapi display, and (A3) an explicit mapping write path. Legacy rows may be evidenced by a quoted model id plus account guard in tk_*.sql or by the served-via-admin-ui seed-state marker; every new floor must declare served-via-modelops-activation and then complete the approved evidence-backed prod activation before release. A3 catches the #812 priced/displayed-but-empty-pool failure without forcing generic deploy to mutate live accounts. Pinning both legacy and activation markers, the selftest, and the allowlist parser prevents an upstream merge from silently dropping either safety path. Wired into preflight and the upstream conflict gate.

The served-models MANIFEST is the single declarative intent source consumed by the drift guard, onboarding skill, display projections, and generated account-mapping bundle. Pinning the schema keys plus the modelops activation declaration prevents an upstream merge from truncating the manifest or reverting new mapping floors to generic-deploy migrations while leaving compile/tests superficially green. Co-located with the overlay so the same preflight parses price and serving intent. account 96 pins the XRToken ch54 Seedance serving intent (two XRToken-only SKUs plus three shared with the Ark pool) so a merge cannot revert the manifest to the Ark-only rows.

The registry loader builds one immutable snapshot containing model prices, catalog metadata, executable policy, and publication metadata. A valid runtime envelope exactly replaces the embedded snapshot; there is no union. Invalid schema/digest/content keeps last-known-good. tkValidateAndBuildOverlayVideoTiers rejects malformed billing ladders before swap, TokenPricingAbsent preserves media/token settlement separation, and SupportsReasoning anchors catalog capability projection.

Focused runtime-overlay regression evidence: malformed video ladders must be rejected before a hot swap, while an omitted compatibility default is deterministically derived from the tier row marked default_for_model.

Protected publisher contract: sync-runtime must load the exact current origin/main registry, require HEAD and workspace bytes to match, build a schema/commit/exact-byte digest envelope, and verify post-write provenance plus exact content with post.is_current. Read-only audit may accept content-current provenance lag, but publisher no-op and post-write success remain strict. Arbitrary local files and unmerged branches cannot become global runtime owners.

Runtime hot-reload wiring for the complete registry: reloadTKOverlayRuntime validates the protected-main envelope before atomically replacing prices, policy, metadata, and catalog inputs; corruption keeps last-known-good. SubscribeOverlayRuntime reloads replicas on settings_updated and SetOverlayRuntimeDeps preserves the upstream constructor. Dropping these hooks turns protected hot publication into a silent no-op until the next application release.

Wire boundary for the complete registry runtime setting. The setting getter, initial reload, and cross-replica subscription must remain forced into the server graph without changing the upstream PricingService constructor.

Admin GET /admin/accounts/:id/models for Gemini routes through tkGeminiAdminAvailableModels (model_mapping SSOT). Non-Google-One accounts still intersect mapping with ServableClientFacingIDs via tkGeminiAdminModelsForMapping; Google One keeps the conservative whitelist from GetModelMapping without servable pruning. Every platform projects package-specific metadata through tkAdminModelOptions into the same []dto.AccountModelOption HTTP contract. Governed custom-account create/update/re-test lifecycle events must schedule one account+revision candidate-set probe job; that job evaluates Chat Completions, Responses, and native Anthropic Messages before one complete-set CAS write.

must_contain: unservable mapped preview must not appear
response must expose only id and display_name
sentinels.rationale: Regression guards for Gemini mapping ∩ servable behavior and the exact two-field response contract across every first-class account platform. Upstream merges that rewrite the handler/tests must fail if they re-advertise an unservable Gemini id or leak platform-specific model fields.

must_contain: return nil, fmt.Errorf("read model availability for %s/%s: %w"
sentinels.rationale: Automatic-key discovery fallback uses the same servable catalog as pricing, but unlike storefront rendering it must surface availability repository errors. This strict companion preserves structurally-gone pruning and priced membership without converting an unknown repository state into a successful capability menu.
